stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Skewed positive view from omitted caveats.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con «What is missing.» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: Skewed positive view from omitted caveats

options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes
mistakes a surface feature of "Page count" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: omitting caveats skews the view positive; option A captures that. On that basis "Skewed positive view from omitted caveats" is the supported choice. Option B ("Random variation") fails because it confuses omission with chance; Option C ("Chart color") fails because it substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for bias shown by omission; Option D ("Page count") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "Page count" for the governing rule.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A causal claim from a correlation

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Ads cause all sales.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Reverse causation.». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.misconception: treats "Data needs review" as if it followed from the evidence

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: correlation does not prove causation; demand may drive ads. On that basis "Ads cause all sales" is the supported choice. Option A ("Data needs review") fails because it treats "Data needs review" as if it followed from the evidence; Option B ("Demand drives ad spending") fails because it sound explanation; Option C ("Both vary by season") fails because it true but not the flaw.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A conclusion that widens the claim

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «This design suits every user.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «span-4.7-0059», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: These nine users liked the design.
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "These nine users liked the design" for the governing rule
reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out
selects "More testing is needed" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: extending nine users to every user overgeneralizes; option A does that. On that basis "This design suits every user" is the supported choice. Option B ("These nine users liked the design") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "These nine users liked the design" for the governing rule; Option C ("The pilot had nine users") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles a conclusion that widens the claim; Option D ("More testing is needed") fails because it selects "More testing is needed" where a conclusion that widens the claim requires a different condition.
